summary.intent: Take on the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze the confidential supplier/launch data, then build a general recheck-and-act agent product (poller, extraction, recompute, supplier actions, Today/Launch/Routines UI) before the Sunday 12:00 hand-in.
summary.outcome: Found that Soony's plan hid real shortfalls (art books overbooked 80,000 vs 8,000, failed statue lot, frozen tracker, clear cases, card shortfall) and built a working app with a versioned poller, case cards, supplier email actions, routines, a drop drill and many UX fixes. Art book order was confirmed by Karton; hand-in material (README, demo script, video, pitch) and the push remain.

repo: Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder; .env holds SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN and is gitignored, .env.example is committed.

The portal API has only GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path} and /archive.zip, with no webhook or notifications. Drops must be detected by polling and comparing SHA-256, and existing files get replaced under the same name.
Team workflow is in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; work is on branch jonas/today-flow with many unpushed commits.
Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files changed; with no changes its turn-end logs 'no files modified during session, skipping checkpoint'.
Safe rehearsal pattern: run a second server on a copy of data/portal, state and store with ASK_REPLY_POLL=off, ASK_TEAMS=off, ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none so nothing polls, mails or calls for real.
Supplier profile addresses must not be trusted as send targets until a person confirms a new contact (supplier_addresses and supplier_email follow this rule).
Prepared routine proposals must expire when their case is decided, and the same step for the same case is deduplicated across routines.
ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK is empty, so Hamburg questions went out only as push notifications; internal messages and escalations are only recorded, with no delivery channel.

code.finding: Routine diagram was rewritten to three groups (When, one 'Only if' node with numbered checklist and funnel counts, Then steps) with n8n-style node cards and connectors only between groups.
Computes per-condition remaining counts in the browser by copying routines.py matching logic, so counts can drift from the server and are approximate for waiting/replies triggers.
Delay notices with a new date now count as late, and papercheck no longer auto-resolves cards while an input it used to read is unreadable (tracked in papercheck_reads.json).
New module comparing newer supplier profiles with profile.csv (status, qualification, expiry, contact) to raise cards; wired into the state build in api.py.
Tracker file choice now takes the highest version, then the newest file, instead of first in sort order.
Option matching searched a literal 'make po,rev' string instead of 'make po' and 'rev', so a routine found its case but sent nothing; fixed and tested.

workflow: Put the first thin version of the act step in the product rather than hand-replying to suppliers, since judges score agents that take real actions.
Use subagents for long cross-checks (200 order confirmations, 59 scans) and UX redesigns, then verify screenshots and commit the results.
Check the browser (screenshots, simulated J key presses) before committing UI fixes.
Avoid committing partial work: a commit that picked up api.py changes without the new supplier_master.py module would not start, so commit topic by topic and run tests.
Replies to side emails should not close the case they are logged on; they add information but do not decide anything.

friction: Portal token was initially empty, so the API returned 401 and blocked data work until it was set.
Data drops arrive without notice (five files within 37 minutes), so the 14:00 analysis went stale quickly.
A commit accidentally included api.py changes without supplier_master.py, so that commit alone would not start.
Replies to manual tracking questions wrongly marked three cases as sent and removed them from 'Needs you'; they had to be reopened.
The routine option-matching bug meant an enabled routine did nothing, and routines showed 'not run yet' after being switched on.
Stale prepared proposals ('Do all 4') failed with 'not an open card', and a duplicate routine produced duplicate steps.
The left list did not scroll, and selecting a decided case jumped the list back to the top.
Launch said 'Decide by' even when the case was with Maren.
PackRight received extra rev C requests after already answering, and the Pulse email to a non-existent address bounced.
Unknown whether portal data and actions are the same across teams; this was not documented.
open_items: Push the unpushed commits on jonas/today-flow (about 25) once the user approves.
Write the README, 3-minute demo script, video and pitch for the 12:00 hand-in.
Decide whether to merge the four 'Are there really…' count questions into one case; 17 cases in 'Needs you' is a lot.
Route internal messages and escalations through push and Teams, and make the UI say honestly where they went.
Set up the Teams incoming webhook and put ASK_TEAMS_WEBHOOK in .env (user must do this).
Delete the duplicate routine 'Ask Hamburg to count book stock'.
Send the note to Hwaseong and the message to Lucas about the Pulse emails.
Register sender email addresses in portal Settings and decide on a team inbox for sending and replies.
Decide whether to delete the earlier Claude doc now that the page exists.
Change the Today header to show the next decision deadline (e.g. 'next decision by 09:00').
The art book truck is estimated to arrive after the cell runs dry (~11:16); a follow-up case for a direct van, split load or pickup is needed.
A real predictor (news impact) run was untested, and the memo's 'Quality last word' and 'air/rush to CPO within the hour' rules are not yet used for routing.
Next PackRight email should send the rev C file and change notice and ask how much of the order is unprinted, rather than repeating the revision request.
Ask the Lio engineers whether portal data is identical across teams and whether supplier replies create portal files.
